subject: Requesting custom SLA addendum + evidence for MSA (Meditrace)
messages:
From: Natalie Cho <natalie.cho@meditrace.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@meditrace.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: Custom SLA addendum + evidence for MSA (Meditrace)

Hi David,

Thanks for the quick walk-through earlier. Procurement and engineering at Meditrace reviewed the standard MSA and would like to request a bespoke SLA addendum tied to our enterprise order form before legal signs. High-level asks from our side:

- Availability: target 99.995% monthly for our primary US region with an explicit regional fallback plan.
- Latency: p50/p90 for text-generation API (200ms/350ms) for sequences <=512 tokens; we understand this varies by model but need guardrails.
- Credits/financial remedy schedule for degraded window (we can provide suggested language).
- Evidence: full one-month historical availability logs, latency histograms (p50/p90/p99) for the model variants you propose, and the KV-cache effectiveness report if available.

Attached is the current redline of our MSA (Meditrace_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf). Procurement also flagged a need to see a proposed order-form annex (SLA language) and clarity on how exceptions are handled for scheduled maintenance vs emergent incidents.

Can you confirm what evidence you can provide and an estimated lead time to produce the Order Form SLA Annex draft? We prefer to bundle the annex with the order form for signature via DocuSign.

Best,
Natalie Cho
Head of Vendor Ops | Meditrace Health
---
Attachment: Meditrace_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf (pdf, 412KB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Cho <natalie.cho@meditrace.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: Custom SLA addendum + evidence for MSA (Meditrace)

Natalie,

Appreciate the clear ask and the redlines — that's very helpful. Short answers up front:

- Evidence: we can produce 30 days of availability telemetry for the proposed cluster, latency histograms (p50/p90/p99) by model variant, and a KV cache hit-rate summary. We will not publish raw customer payloads — all evidence will be telemetry/metrics and anonymized request counts.
- Order form language: we will draft an SLA Annex that maps to your availability and latency asks, plus a credits schedule for degraded windows.
- Exceptions: we'll include a schedule for planned maintenance (72‑hour notification preferred when possible) and an incident-classification table to distinguish emergent incidents eligible for credits.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus and I will put together the evidence bundle and a first-pass SLA Annex by EOD Friday (2027-04-23).
2) If that looks OK, we can route the annex into your procurement DocuSign envelope; legal redlines can be handled on the MSA and annex in parallel.
3) If you and procurement prefer, schedule a 30-min call Friday morning to run through the credits and the incident-classification table.

Two quick clarifications we need from your side:
- Is Meditrace planning to use Redwood Dedicated capacity in us-east for this purchase (this drives the availability targets and fallback design)?
- Are there any specific encryption/KMS or SOC2 evidence requirements beyond standard reports?

I'll attach the evidence checklist and the internal Ops notes for Marcus.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Desk: +1 415-555-0134

Attachment: internal-evidence-checklist.txt (txt, 4KB)

From: Natalie Cho <natalie.cho@meditrace.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@meditrace.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: Custom SLA addendum + evidence for MSA (Meditrace)

David, Marcus — thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifications from procurement/engineering: 

- Yes, we intend to purchase Dedicated capacity in us-east as our primary region, with us-west as fallback.
- KMS: we require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for model payloads at rest; please confirm integrations (AWS KMS & HashiCorp Vault).
- SOC2: a copy of the current SOC2 Type II report or the SOC2 auditor contact is necessary.

Procurement attached a short workbook with the items they'd like to see in the evidence bundle and some suggested wording for credits (see Procurement_SLA_Questions.xlsx). Also, we have a few non-standard asks:
  * A clause that defines a degraded-mode operational window where traffic is routed to lower-cost model variants with prior notice; financial remediation should differ if auto-fallback is used.
  * A 15-day remediation window to provide post-incident root cause analysis for Sev 1 incidents.

We are targeting signature by the end of the month; if you can get the annex and evidence bundle to us by Friday EOD, we can try to close next week.

Thanks,
Natalie

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Cho <natalie.cho@meditrace.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: Custom SLA addendum + evidence for MSA (Meditrace)

Natalie — forwarding the draft annex and evidence plan for your review. See the attached OrderForm_SLA_Annex.docx which includes:

- Availability definition (region-bound): monthly uptime % with formulas and measurement method (heartbeat + synthetic checks).
- Latency SLOs by model family with measurement windows and sample size requirements.
- Credits schedule tiered by severity and duration; special handling for auto-fallback events.
- Incident timeline requirements: initial notification within 1 hour, root cause and RCA within 15 days for Sev 1.
- Exceptions: scheduled maintenance, force majeure, and customer-caused degradation.

We can support customer-managed KMS in our Private deployment; for Redwood Dedicated we support AWS KMS with CMKs and a Vault integration — I'll loop infra if you want a short technical deep-dive. The SOC2 Type II report is available under NDA; I'll send the auditor contact via a secure link and include a redacted summary in the evidence bundle.

If this draft aligns with your procurement workbook, happy to lock in a 30-minute call today at 1pm ET to walk through the credits table and the fallback wording.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
